assessment.summary: ABL1 is one of the most extensively validated and successfully drugged kinase targets in oncology, with 7 approved drugs including imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib, and bosutinib, primarily for BCR-ABL1-driven chronic myeloid leukemia. Structural characterization is exceptional, with 85 PDB entries at resolutions as low as 1.03Å and the majority of top structures containing bound ligands. Chemical and literature evidence is among the strongest available for any human kinase target.
evidence_gaps: AlphaFold mean pLDDT of 63.4 is relatively low, but this is superseded by extensive experimental PDB structures and is likely reflective of disordered regulatory regions (e.g., SH3/SH2 linkers, N-terminal cap) rather than the kinase domain itself
Resistance mutations (e.g., T315I gatekeeper) remain a clinical challenge; coverage of all clinically relevant mutant structures may be incomplete
Selectivity profiles across the full kinome for all 7 approved drugs are not fully detailed in the provided evidence
Emerging roles of ABL1 in non-oncology contexts (e.g., neurological, cardiovascular) are underexplored relative to the CML focus
Allosteric binding sites beyond the ATP pocket and myristoyl pocket may not be fully structurally characterized
